question: Of the laws in force, which write the sanction as a consequence and which as a power, and has either been used once?

laws.name: EU AI Act, duties of model providers
laws.note: The fine is the Commission's to impose or not. The power to fine began a year after the duties it sanctions. The Commission's enforcement page, last updated 2026-10-20, names no provider, no proceeding and no fine; a law firm's note reports first requests for information on 2026-08-29, which this study did not find on a Commission page.

laws.name: California SB 53
laws.note: The penalty follows from the breach, but only the Attorney General can take it to a court. His office has an investigation of OpenAI on record, with a subpoena served on 2026-09-30; the release names no statute, so it cannot be counted as a use of this act. No civil action under the act was found.

laws.name: US export controls (ECRA and the export regulations)
laws.body: Department of Justice; Bureau of Industry and Security
laws.applicable_since: 2018 (the act); chips controlled later by rule
laws.note: Both moods: prison and a fine follow from a willful breach, and the Secretary may add a civil penalty. Five announcements between August 2025 and October 2026 charge 13 people and one company over AI chips; one man and his company pleaded guilty, to smuggling and unlawful export activities as the release words it. No sentence and no civil penalty over AI chips was found on the pages read.

uses.what: criminal complaint: GPUs exported to China without a licence through a small company (ALX Solutions Inc.)
indictment: GPUs transshipped to China through Malaysia and Thailand, a front company in Florida
guilty pleas of 2025-10-10 to smuggling and unlawful export activities (at least $160 million of H100 and H200 chips); over $50 million seized
two more charged in the same network, one with conspiring to violate the export act, one with conspiring to smuggle
indictment: servers with AI chips diverted to China; the export agency's annual report calls the three Super Micro executives
indictment: more than $300 million of servers with GPUs sent to China through Malaysia and Singapore
investigation of security incidents at OpenAI, subpoena served 2026-09-30; the release names no statute

a civil action by California's Attorney General under SB 53 (web search, 2026-11-11; the Attorney General's press releases as returned by search)
a sentence in a US case over AI chips, among them the sentencing set for 2026-02-18 (web search, 2026-11-11)

a third guilty plea, in October 2026, in the case of 2026-03-19 (a news agency, citing a court filing)

predictions.text: The AI Act writes its fines for model providers as a power of the Commission, applicable later than the duties.
predictions.result: held: Article 101 says the Commission "may impose"; Article 113 applies the duties from 2 August 2025 "with the exception of Article 101", which followed on 2 August 2026. Not predicted: for other breaches the same act writes "shall be subject to administrative fines"

predictions.text: California's SB 53 writes its civil penalty as a consequence, gated: only the Attorney General may bring the action.
predictions.result: held, on a text read through a page-fetch service: "shall be subject to a civil penalty", recovered "in a civil action brought only by the Attorney General"

predictions.text: US export law holds both: a criminal clause written as a consequence and a civil clause written as a power.
predictions.result: held: "shall be fined" and "shall be imprisoned" for a willful breach; "The Secretary may impose" civil penalties

predictions.text: No record found of any sanction imposed under the AI Act's provisions for model providers or under SB 53.
predictions.result: held, as no record found: the Commission's enforcement page names no provider and no fine; no action by California's Attorney General under the act was found. Not predicted: his office is investigating OpenAI and served a subpoena on 2026-09-30, under no statute the release names

predictions.text: Export controls have been used on compute at least once: a charge or penalty over advanced AI chips, 2025 or 2026.
predictions.result: held: five announcements of the Department of Justice between 2025-08-05 and 2026-10-01, 13 people and one company; two guilty pleas. Not predicted: no sentence and no civil penalty over AI chips was found, and the export agency's own tables for fiscal 2025 list none

predictions.text: No sanction under the three laws fell on a holder of the step-1 record or a developer of frontier models; export cases hit intermediaries.
predictions.result: held for sanctions and charges: the 14 parties are individuals and one small company. One developer of frontier models, OpenAI, stands under an inquiry. Not as predicted in one respect: three of the charged are described by the export agency as executives of a large server maker, not a shell
